en: Taal Volcano features a crater lake on Volcano Island, which is situated right in the middle of the much larger Taal Lake.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan flows directly into the sea, making its lower portion subject to the ocean's tidal changes.
Bohol’s famous Chocolate Hills consist of exactly 1,268 cone-shaped mounds that turn brown during the dry season, resembling giant chocolate kisses.
The Cagayan River is the longest in the Philippines, stretching approximately 505 kilometers through the Cagayan Valley before emptying into the Pacific Ocean.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park is a protected UNESCO World Heritage site located in the very center of the Sulu Sea.
Because it sits inside the Pacific Typhoon Belt, the Philippines experiences an average of 20 tropical cyclones every single year.
The Philippine Trench, located east of the archipelago, is the country's deepest oceanic point, plunging to a depth of 10,540 meters.
If the stone walls of the Banaue Rice Terraces were stretched out end-to-end, they would encircle approximately half of the globe.
The Verde Island Passage, located between Batangas and Mindoro, is scientifically recognized as the center of the world's marine shorefish biodiversity.
Mayon Volcano in Albay province is globally famous for possessing the most perfectly symmetrical natural volcanic cone in the entire world.
Lake Mainit, situated on the boundary of Agusan del Norte and Surigao del Norte, is the deepest lake in the Philippines.
The Cordillera Administrative Region contains the highest concentration of towering peaks in the Philippines, including the country's second-highest mountain, Mount Pulag.
